url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/watch.md
---
# Watch

The `watch` section configures `dbx watch`, which syncs once and then re-runs on
input changes.

```ts [dbx.config.ts]
export default defineConfig({
    toolchain: {
        watch: { enabled: true, debounce: 150 },
    },
});
```

## Options

| Option      | Type                 | Default              | Description                                 |
| ----------- | -------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled`   | `boolean`            | enabled when defined | Watch by default.                           |
| `debounce`  | `number`             | `150`                | Debounce window in ms before a re-sync.     |
| `exclude`   | `string \| string[]` | common ignored paths | Glob(s) excluded from watching.             |
| `gitignore` | `boolean`            | `true`               | Respect `.gitignore` files (root + nested). |

`exclude` adds to the common ignored paths (`node_modules`, `.dbx`, `dist`,
`build`, ...), and `gitignore` also honours the repo's `.gitignore` files (root
and nested, each scoped to its own directory) so ignored directories are never
watched. Set `gitignore: false` to watch them anyway.

```ts
watch: { exclude: ['**/fixtures/**'], gitignore: true }
```

## How it works

```sh
dbx watch
```

`dbx watch` runs one sync, then watches the config file plus every task's
`watch` globs and re-runs on change. Writes made by the sync itself must not
re-trigger a run, so a short quiet window follows each sync.

Only **input** files are watched (eg. `dbx.config.*`, `tsconfig.default.json`,
`tsconfig.workspaces.json`), never the generated outputs — so a sync can never
loop on its own writes.

`dbx watch --force` runs even when there is no `dbx.config.*`, and
`watch: { enabled: false }` disables it (so a plain `dbx watch` warns and exits).

## VS Code

The VS Code extension has its own debounced scheduler that mirrors this
behaviour (see [VS Code Extension](/guide/vscode#auto-sync)); the `watch` section
configures the **CLI** `dbx watch` command.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/logger.md
---
# Logger

Every toolchain message goes through one logger, so output stays consistent and
respects a single configuration. The `logger` section controls its level,
colours and prefix.

```ts [dbx.config.ts]
export default defineConfig({
    toolchain: {
        logger: { level: 'debug', color: false, name: 'dbx' },
    },
});
```

## Options

| Option     | Type                                               | Default | Description                                            |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `level`    | `debug` | `info` | `warn` | `error` | `silent` | `info`  | Minimum level to print.                                |
| `color`    | `boolean`                                          | `true`  | Force colours on/off.                                  |
| `name`     | `string`                                           | `dbx`   | Prefix for non-indented lines.                         |
| `suppress` | `string \| string[]`                               | none    | Silence warnings/errors by id, substring or `/regex/`. |

Colour is **on by default** (the toolchain forces it rather than relying on TTY
autodetection); `--no-color` or `logger: { color: false }` turn it off. Human
output is rendered with [`@clack/prompts`](https://bombshell.dev/clack) — level
symbols (`•` info, `◆` success, `▲` warn, `■` error) and a guide.

## CLI overrides

| Flag                | Description                                                |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--log-level <lvl>` | Minimum level: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `silent`. |
| `--color`           | Force coloured output (the default).                       |
| `--no-color`        | Disable coloured output.                                   |

They win over the config and may appear before or after the subcommand.

## Machine output

`--json` (and provider passthroughs) write raw, unprefixed, undecorated output
through the same logger (`logger.raw`), so it is safe to pipe into `jq` or
another tool.

## Providers

Provider passthrough commands (Vite+) follow the logger's colour setting, and the
[`providers`](/guide/providers#colour) section can force provider colours on or
off independently. `color: false` runs the wrapped binary with `NO_COLOR=1` and
`FORCE_COLOR=0`.

## Programmatic API

```ts
import {
    configureLogger,
    createLogger,
    getLogger,
    isLogLevel,
    logger,
    normalizeLogLevel,
    setLogConfig,
    setLogOverrides,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain/shared';
```

| Export                             | Description                                            |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `logger`                           | The active logger (delegates to the current instance). |
| `createLogger(options?)`           | Build a logger with explicit options.                  |
| `setLogConfig(section)`            | Apply the `logger` config section.                     |
| `setLogOverrides(options)`         | Apply CLI overrides (win over the config).             |
| `configureLogger(options?)`        | Alias for `setLogOverrides`.                           |
| `isLogLevel` / `normalizeLogLevel` | Validate/coerce a level.                               |

Use `logger.info` for human messages and `logger.raw` for machine output; avoid
`console.log` so output stays consistent and respects the config and CLI flags.

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/providers.md
---
# Providers

A **provider** is an external toolchain exposed through `dbx`: its CLI,
the programmatic API and the VS Code extension. Providers contribute namespaced
commands and a descriptor the editor reads over `dbx providers --json`.

## List providers

```sh
dbx providers          # table
dbx providers --json   # descriptor (id, binary, commands, actions)
```

## Vite+ (`vite-plus`)

The bundled provider wraps the `vp` binary — the unified Vite / Vitest / Oxlint /
Oxfmt / Rolldown / tsdown toolchain.

### Resolution

`dbx vite:*` resolves `vp` in this order:

1. the project-local shim (`node_modules/.bin/vp`),
2. a global `vp` on `PATH`,
3. `npx --yes vite-plus`.

### Generic passthrough

```sh
dbx vite dev
dbx vite build
dbx vite add zod
dbx vite check
```

Everything after `vite` is forwarded verbatim to `vp`, so all Vite+ commands and
flags are reachable. A bare `dbx <command>` whose name is a Vite+ command (or a
Vite+ alias) is forwarded too, so `dbx fmt` / `dbx run -r build` need no `vite`
namespace — built-in commands win (`dbx migrate` stays the toolchain's).

### Colour

Provider output keeps `vp`'s own colours, but follows the logger's colour state.
The global `--no-color` flag turns provider colour off, and the `providers`
section can opt out on its own even on a colour terminal:

```ts [dbx.config.ts]
export default defineConfig({
    toolchain: {
        providers: { color: false },
    },
});
```

When colour is off, `dbx` runs `vp` with `NO_COLOR=1` and `FORCE_COLOR=0` so the
wrapped process emits plain output. Leave the section unset to let `vp` detect
colour from its own terminal.

### Named commands

Every catalogued subcommand is also available as a first-class command for
discovery + the editor:

```
vite:create  vite:migrate  vite:dev  vite:check  vite:lint  vite:fmt  vite:test
vite:build   vite:pack     vite:run  vite:add    vite:remove vite:update ...
vite:toolchain vite:upgrade vite:implode
```

### Programmatic

```ts
import {
    resolveVp,
    runVp,
    hasVp,
    vpVersion,
    describeVp,
    resolveVpCommand,
    viteCommandName,
    VP_COMMANDS,
} from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';

if (hasVp(process.cwd())) {
    await runVp(['check'], { cwd: process.cwd() });
}
```

| Export                                 | Description                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `resolveVp(cwd?)`                      | Resolve the `vp` invocation (`{ exe, args, source }`).                      |
| `hasVp(cwd?)`                          | Whether a local/global `vp` is available (no `npx` fallback).               |
| `runVp(args, options?)`                | Run `vp`, streaming output or `mode: 'capture'`; never exits the host.      |
| `vpVersion(cwd?)` / `describeVp(cwd?)` | The `vp --version` output / a one-line resolution description.              |
| `which(bin)`                           | Find an executable on `PATH` (resolves `PATHEXT` on Windows).               |
| `resolveVpCommand(name)`               | Resolve a subcommand **or alias** to its canonical name (`i` -> `install`). |
| `viteCommandName(name)`                | The `dbx` command name for a `vp` subcommand (`dev` -> `vite:dev`).         |
| `VP_COMMANDS`                          | The `vp` command catalog that drives the CLI + the provider descriptor.     |

```ts
// A bare `dbx <command>` falls through to `vite` when it names a Vite+ command.
resolveVpCommand('fmt'); // 'fmt'
viteCommandName('fmt'); // 'vite:fmt'
```

### Use dbx from Vite+

Vite+ consumers can drive dbx from `vite.config.ts`, so a Vite+-only project
still gets dbx's generated/managed files:

```ts [vite.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from 'vite-plus';

import { dbx, DBX_TASKS } from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';

export default defineConfig({
    plugins: [dbx()],
    run: { tasks: { ...DBX_TASKS } },
    // your usual Vite / Vite+ config
});
```

* The `dbx()` plugin runs `dbx sync` before the dev server / build, or
  `dbx sync --check` in CI (which fails the build when generated files are out of
  date), and re-syncs when a `dbx.config.*` / `tsconfig.*.json` input changes.
* The plugin resolves the `dbx` binary from the project first: the local
  `node_modules/.bin/dbx`, then the project's own `@deltabox/toolchain` bin. A
  global `dbx` on `PATH` is used **only when the project doesn't pin the
  toolchain at all** — otherwise it's skipped (with a warning) in favour of
  `npx @deltabox/toolchain@<pinned>`. That way a stale global install can never
  run and silently revert the project's generated files.
* `run: { tasks: { ...DBX_TASKS } }` also exposes `vp run dbx:sync` /
  `vp run dbx:check`. Vite+ reads `run.tasks` from the **static** config (a
  plugin's `config` hook is ignored), so the tasks are spread in the config
  rather than added by the plugin. Drop the `run` block if you don't want them.
* Because Vite Task runs a task's `command` through a shell, `DBX_TASKS` bakes in
  the binary resolved by `resolveDbx` (the project's own, or the pinned `npx`
  fallback) rather than relying on `dbx` being on `PATH` — a missing environment
  then warns instead of silently running the wrong binary. Use `dbxTaskCommand(sub)`
  to build a task command for another subcommand.

## Custom providers

Providers are loaded from **search paths** (JSON files, directories of
`*.json`, or `http(s)` registry URLs). A JSON file can be an array of provider
descriptors or `{ "providers": [...] }`.

Project paths (first wins on an id clash):

* `.dbx/toolchain/.registry/providers` — the implicit default directory;
* `.dbx/toolchain/registries.json` — its `providers` array;
* `.dbx/toolchain/providers.json` — the legacy file, still read.

Global paths:

* `~/.dbx/toolchain/.registry/providers` — the default directory;
* `~/.dbx/toolchain/cli/config.json` — `providerRegistrySearchPaths`, or
  `registrySearchPaths.providers`;
* the VS Code `deltabox.providerRegistrySearchPaths` setting (kept in sync).

`toolchainProviders()` merges every local registry with the built-ins (a project
provider wins on an id clash), so a custom provider's commands become `dbx`
commands — `dbx <command.name>` forwards to `<binary> <subcommand> ...` — and it
shows up in `dbx providers` and the editor. Remote registries are fetched by
`dbx providers --json`/`loadToolchainProviders()`. Restrict them with
`toolchain.registry.providers` (`allow`/`deny` host + path globs); the same
policy applies to local registry paths:

```json [.dbx/toolchain/.registry/providers/providers.json]
[
    {
        "id": "echo",
        "name": "Echo",
        "binary": "node",
        "commands": [
            {
                "name": "echo:version",
                "subcommand": "--version",
                "description": "Print the Node version"
            }
        ]
    }
]
```

```sh
dbx registry --json                                  # list template + provider paths
dbx registry --kind providers --scope project --add ./providers
dbx registry --kind providers --scope global --add https://example.com/providers.json
```

The VS Code **Providers** view manages the registry items (**Add provider...** /
**Remove provider**), and the **Registries** view shows the provider search
paths. See [VS Code Extension](/guide/vscode).

## Providers in the editor

The VS Code extension reads `providers --json` and builds its **Providers** view
and menus from it, so adding a provider surfaces it automatically. See
[VS Code Extension](/guide/vscode).

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator.md
---
# Config Generator

`@deltabox/toolchain/config` is a generic, Zod-backed configuration engine. A
**Zod schema is the single source of truth**: attach env metadata to leaves with
`.meta()`, then generate the `.env` file, env/config TypeScript types, a JSON
Schema, a markdown reference, config metadata JSON and CLI option definitions —
all from that one schema.

## Where to start

* [Describe a scope](/guide/config-generator/describe-a-scope) — write the Zod
  schema and its `.meta()`.
* [Create the engine](/guide/config-generator/create-the-engine) — bind scopes,
  prefix, base group and root.
* [Generate](/guide/config-generator/generate) — the generator methods.
* [CLI commands](/guide/config-generator/cli-commands) — the `config:*` command
  descriptors.
* [Load the config](/guide/config-generator/load-the-config) — the runtime loader
  (`parseEnvTree`, `compileZodSchema`, and `applyOverrides` from shared).
* [Generated outputs](/guide/config-generator/generated-outputs) — types,
  markdown, env files, JSON Schema and formatting.
* [Real-world shape](/guide/config-generator/real-world-shape) — how a consumer
  binds the engine end-to-end.

```ts
import { createConfigEngine } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';
```

url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/scripts.md

# Package scripts

`dbx` writes files, not your `package.json` — but a few scripts are worth
standardizing, because the toolchain's formatting/linting and task running both
go through **Vite+**. Any bare `dbx <command>` that matches a Vite+ command is
forwarded straight to it (`dbx fmt`, `dbx run -r build`, `dbx dev`), so a project
only needs the one `dbx` command. This page shows the recommended root scripts
and how to move an existing Biome + Turbo project onto them.

## Recommended scripts

The repo root `package.json`:

```json [package.json]
{
    "scripts": {
        "format": "dbx fmt",
        "lint": "dbx lint --fix",
        "check": "dbx check",
        "build": "dbx run -r build",
        "typecheck": "dbx run -r typecheck",
        "test": "dbx run -r test",
        "dbx:sync": "dbx sync",
        "dbx:watch": "dbx watch",
        "commitlint": "commitlint",
        "postinstall": "husky"
    }
}
```

| Script                         | What it does                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `format` / `lint` / `check`    | Oxfmt / Oxlint across the repo (`check` = format check + lint). |
| `build` / `typecheck` / `test` | Runs the task in every workspace, in dependency order.          |
| `dbx:sync` / `dbx:watch`       | Regenerate the managed files / re-sync on change.               |
| `commitlint` / `postinstall`   | Conventional Commits via commitlint + husky.                    |

Notes:

* A bare command that names a Vite+ command is forwarded to Vite+ (`vp`) — eg.
  `dbx fmt`, `dbx dev`, `dbx run -r build`, `dbx add zod` (Vite+ aliases too).
  Built-in commands win, so `dbx migrate` is the toolchain's migration — use
  `dbx vite migrate` for Vite+'s. The explicit `dbx vite <command>` passthrough
  always works.
* Vite+ resolves from the **repo root**, so `format`/`lint` live there — keep
  them out of the individual workspaces.
* `dbx run -r <task>` runs a task in every workspace package in dependency order.
  A task is either a `package.json` script or a `vite.config.ts` `run.tasks`
  entry. For long-running processes use `dbx run -r --parallel dev`.
* `dbx` is the toolchain binary, so `yarn dbx <cmd>` (eg. `yarn dbx sync`) works
  even without a script; the `dbx:*` aliases are just for discoverability.

When `ci.changelog` is enabled, `dbx sync` also writes a husky
`commit-msg` hook (`.husky/commit-msg`) that runs commitlint, so commits are
linted locally as well as in CI. Use `postinstall` (not `prepare`) to activate
husky: Yarn Berry never runs `prepare` on install. Husky hooks have no file
extension, so on Windows add `.husky/* text eol=lf` to `.gitattributes` — a
trailing CR silently breaks the hook.

## Migrate an existing project

1. Add the toolchain + Vite+, and drop what they replace:

   ```diff
   -    "@biomejs/biome": "catalog:",
   -    "turbo": "^2.11.2",
   +    "@deltabox/toolchain": "^1.2.3",
   +    "vite-plus": "^1.2.0",
   ```

2. Fold the Biome config into a root `vite.config.ts`:

   ```sh
   dbx migrate --from biome --target vite --write
   ```

   Or, if the project uses `dbx.config.ts`, author the Vite+ config there under
   `toolchain.vite`. `dbx sync` then writes the root `vite.config.ts` shim (see
   [Vite+](/guide/config/vite)). `dbx migrate --from vite --write` folds an
   existing hand-written `vite.config.ts` in.

3. Replace the scripts (see the tables below), then delete `biome.json` and
   `turbo.json`.

4. Add a `dbx.config.ts` and sync the managed files:

   ```sh
   dbx sync
   ```

5. Verify — this is what CI runs:

   ```sh
   dbx sync --check
   yarn build
   ```

### Biome → Oxc

| Before                   | After            |
| ------------------------ | ---------------- |
| `biome format --write .` | `dbx fmt`        |
| `biome check --fix .`    | `dbx lint --fix` |
| `biome.json`             | `vite.config.ts` |

Remove `@biomejs/biome`, delete `biome.json`, and drop any per-workspace
`format`/`lint` scripts.

### Turbo → Vite Task

| Before            | After                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `turbo build`     | `dbx run -r build`                         |
| `turbo typecheck` | `dbx run -r typecheck`                     |
| `turbo test`      | `dbx run -r test`                          |
| `turbo dev`       | `dbx run -r --parallel dev`                |
| `turbo.json`      | (optional) `run.tasks` in `vite.config.ts` |

Remove `turbo` and `turbo.json`. Ordering comes from each package's
`package.json` dependencies, so no `turbo.json` graph is needed.

## Per-workspace tasks

For cached, dependency-aware tasks, define them in each package's
`dbx.config.*` rather than `package.json` — a task and a script cannot share a
name:

```ts [packages/<pkg>/dbx.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@deltabox/toolchain';

export default defineConfig({
    toolchain: {
        vite: {
            run: {
                tasks: {
                    build: {
                        command: 'tsdown --config-loader unrun',
                        cache: { input: [{ auto: true }, '!dist/**'], output: ['dist/**'] },
                    },
                    test: {
                        command: 'vitest run',
                        cache: { input: [{ auto: true }], output: [] },
                    },
                },
            },
        },
    },
});
```

See the [Monorepo guide](/guide/monorepo) for the full task setup,
[Migrations](/guide/migrations) for the `dbx migrate` reference, and
[Providers (Vite+)](/guide/providers) for the `dbx vite` passthrough.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/templates.md
---
# Templates

Templates scaffold projects, workspaces, applications, folders, tooling or
pipelines. They can be **offline** (builtin, or a local `template.json`
directory) or **online** (npm `@scope/create` manifests, git repos, and Vite+
templates).

## Kinds

Every template declares a `kind`, used by `template:list --kind` and
`create --kind`:

| Kind          | Produces                               |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `project`     | A single-package project.              |
| `workspace`   | A package inside an existing monorepo. |
| `application` | A runnable application package.        |
| `folder`      | A bare folder of files.                |
| `tooling`     | Toolchain config/pipeline files.       |
| `pipeline`    | A CI/pipeline template.                |

## List + create

```sh
dbx template:list
dbx template:list --kind application   # filter by kind
dbx template:list --online             # also resolve npm/git sources
dbx template:list --registry           # only the .dbx/toolchain sources
dbx template:list --json               # machine-readable (used by the editor)

dbx create --template project --name my-app --out ./my-app
dbx create --kind folder --name scratch --out ./scratch
dbx create --template mytpl --name acme --var port=4000
```

With no `--template`, `create --kind <kind>` picks the first matching template.
An unlisted `--template` id is treated as a Vite+ template (`vp create <id>`).
On an interactive terminal, a bare `dbx create` (no `--template`/`--kind`/`--name`)
prompts for the template, name and scope instead (Ctrl-C cancels).

## Builtin templates

| id                      | Kind          | Description                                    |
| ----------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `project`               | `project`     | A single-package TypeScript project.           |
| `application`           | `application` | A runnable application package.                |
| `folder`                | `folder`      | A bare folder (a README).                      |
| `monorepo`              | `project`     | A monorepo root (no example workspace).        |
| `monorepo-example`      | `project`     | A monorepo root + one example workspace.       |
| `workspace`             | `workspace`   | A workspace package into an existing monorepo. |
| `vite-plus`             | `project`     | `vp create` (interactive or templated).        |
| `vite-plus-monorepo`    | `project`     | `vp create vite:monorepo`.                     |
| `vite-plus-application` | `application` | `vp create vite:application`.                  |
| `vite-plus-library`     | `project`     | `vp create vite:library`.                      |
| `vite-plus-generator`   | `project`     | `vp create vite:generator` (monorepo only).    |

The offline builtins (`project`, `application`, `folder`, `monorepo`,
`monorepo-example`, `workspace`) scaffold a generic, current project: a
`dbx.config.ts` with only `project` metadata, a `package.json` that depends on
`@deltabox/toolchain`, and no Turbo (Vite Task replaces it). They ask for a
**package manager** (default `yarn`) and write that manager's catalog file (see
[Catalogs](/guide/project#package-manager-and-catalogs)). The `vite-plus*` builtins
delegate to `vp create` and need network access.

## Inputs (variables)

A template can declare **inputs** — values prompted for (and substituted) when it
is scaffolded. Declare them in `template.json`:

```json [template.json]
{
    "variables": [
        { "name": "name", "prompt": "Project name", "default": "app", "required": true },
        { "name": "port", "prompt": "Dev port", "default": "4000" },
        { "name": "includeDocker", "prompt": "Include a Dockerfile?", "options": ["yes", "no"] }
    ]
}
```

* `name` — the token name (also `{{ name }}` in files).
* `prompt` — the prompt text (defaults to the name).
* `default` — the value used when nothing is entered.
* `options` — a fixed list of choices: the value is picked from a select.
* `required` — whether a value must be provided.

Files and directory names may contain `{{ token }}` placeholders, resolved while
copying:

```
src/{{name}}.ts   ->   src/acme.ts
```

The **same input pipeline** runs everywhere:

* **CLI** — `dbx create` prompts for each input on an interactive terminal (the
  standard `name`/`scope` first, then the template's own inputs). Pass
  `--var key=value` (repeatable) to skip a prompt.
* **Programmatic API** — `scaffoldTemplate(template, { cwd, tokens, variables })`.
* **VS Code** — **Create from template…** prompts for each input (a quick pick
  when `options` is set).

The builtin templates use the same pipeline (they declare `name`, `scope`,
`packageManager` and `includeConfig` inputs).

## Actions

After the files are written, a template can run **actions** — extra steps such as
installing dependencies. Declare them in `template.json`:

```json [template.json]
{
    "actions": [
        { "id": "install", "prompt": "Install dependencies?", "builtin": "install" },
        { "id": "setup", "prompt": "Run the setup script?", "module": "action.mjs" },
        { "id": "post", "command": "node scripts/post-scaffold.mjs" }
    ]
}
```

* `id` — the action id (also the `--action <id>` key).
* `prompt` — the prompt text (defaults to `Run <id>?`).
* `default` — whether it runs by default (**default false** — opt-in).
* `builtin` — a built-in action. `install` runs `<packageManager> install` in the
  output directory.
* `module` — a JS module (relative to the template directory) whose default
  export is `async (ctx) => void`. The module is **not** copied to the output.
  The context is `{ cwd, templateDir, tokens, variables, packageManager, log }`.
* `command` — a shell command run in the output directory.

Actions run through the same pipeline everywhere: the CLI prompts (or takes
`--action <id>`, repeatable), the extension prompts, and the programmatic API
passes `actions: string[]` to `scaffoldTemplate`. The builtin templates declare
an opt-in **Install dependencies?** action (`builtin: 'install'`, off by
default).

## Local templates

A local template is a directory with a `template.json`. Turn any folder into one
with `template:init` (and register it in one step with `--add`):

```sh
dbx template:init ./templates/acme-service \
  --kind application --name "Acme service" --var name --tag service --add
```

```json [template.json]
{
    "name": "Acme service",
    "description": "A service package",
    "kind": "application",
    "tags": ["service"],
    "variables": [{ "name": "name", "default": "service" }],
    "ignore": ["fixtures"]
}
```

Register sources so they are picked up automatically:

```sh
dbx template:add ./templates             # local dir (auto-inits if needed)
dbx template:add @acme/create            # npm @scope/create
dbx template:add git:https://github.com/acme/tpl.git
dbx template:remove local:./templates    # drop a source
```

`template:add` records them in `.dbx/toolchain/templates.json`; `template:remove`
takes an id or a `type:locate` key. Sources can also be declared in the config:

```ts [dbx.config.ts]
export default defineConfig({
    toolchain: {
        templates: {
            sources: [
                { type: 'local', locate: './templates', kind: 'application' },
                { type: 'npm', locate: '@acme/create', online: true },
            ],
        },
    },
});
```

## Global templates

A template registered with `template:init --add` or `template:add` is **also**
stored in the global registry at `~/.dbx/toolchain/.registry/templates`, so it is
available in every project (and in the VS Code extension). Pass `--no-global` to
keep it project-only:

```sh
dbx template:init ./templates/acme --kind application --name "Acme" --add  # local + global
dbx template:add ./templates --no-global                                  # project only
```

Global templates are merged with the project's own; a project template wins on an
id clash. The global search paths default to
`~/.dbx/toolchain/.registry/templates`, and each path may be a directory or an
`http(s)` **remote registry** (a JSON `{ "sources": [...] }` or an array of
sources):

```sh
dbx template:registry                         # list the resolved paths
dbx template:registry --add ~/shared/templates --add https://acme.dev/templates.json
dbx template:registry --set ~/shared/templates
dbx template:registry --remove ~/shared/templates
dbx template:registry --clear                 # reset to the default
```

The paths live in the CLI config `~/.dbx/toolchain/cli/config.json`
(`registrySearchPaths`, a string or array) and are kept in sync with the VS Code
setting `deltabox.registrySearchPaths`: the extension records the VS Code user
dir in that config and mirrors setting changes into it, and the CLI writes the
setting back when you change the paths. `vscodeDir` in the CLI config points at
the VS Code user directory (the one containing `settings.json`).

The project-scoped registries are stored in `.dbx/toolchain/registries.json` and
default to `.dbx/toolchain/.registry/templates`. `dbx registry [--json]` lists
the detected template/provider registries, and `dbx registry --add <path> --scope global|project` (or `--remove`) manages them. A remote (`http(s)`)
registry is a JSON `{ "sources": [...] }` / array of sources. The VS Code
**Registries** view (below **Templates**) shows the Providers/Templates roots
with **New registry…** / **Remove registry…** actions; remote registries open in
the browser. `dbx template:remove --global <id>` removes a stored global
template.

## Online templates

Online sources are resolved with `--online` (or `dbx template:add`):

* **npm** — a published create package whose `package.json` has a
  `createConfig.templates` (or `dbx.templates`) manifest. Scoped
  (`@acme/create`) and unscoped (`create-acme`, `acme-create`) packages are
  supported; individual templates are listed and created through `vp create`.
  The registry defaults to the project package manager's registry
  (`.yarnrc.yml` `npmRegistryServer`, `.npmrc` `registry`, ...). Override it
  per source with `--registry`:

  ```sh
  dbx template:add @acme/create
  dbx template:add create-acme
  dbx template:add create-acme --registry https://registry.example.com
  ```

* **git** — a repository (optionally with a `ref` and/or `subdir`) listed as a
  template and created through `vp create`:

  ```sh
  dbx template:add git:https://github.com/acme/templates --ref v1.2.0 --subdir apps/web
  ```

* **remote** — an `http(s)` JSON source registry (`{ sources }`, `{ templates }`
  or an array of sources). Its sources are merged into the registry; each is
  then loaded by its own type:

  ```sh
  dbx template:add remote:https://example.com/dbx-templates.json
  ```

* **Vite+** — set `create.defaultTemplate` in the `dbx.config.*`'s `vite` section (the full Vite+
  config) to make a scope the default for `vp create`.

Sources and registries can be restricted with host/path globs (checked for local
paths and remote URLs, which also guards SSRF):

```ts [dbx.config.ts]
toolchain: {
    registry: {
        templates: {
            allow: ['*.example.com', 'https://registry.example.com/**', '**/templates/**'],
            deny: ['*.internal.example.com'],
        },
    },
}
```

## VS Code

The extension drives the same CLI: **From template…** runs `template:list --json`
then `create`; **Add template…** runs `template:init --add` on a folder you pick
and asks whether to add it to the **global** registry (yes by default);
**Remove template…** runs `template:list --registry` then `template:remove`. The
`deltabox.registrySearchPaths` setting controls the global search paths (see
[Global templates](#global-templates)).

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/migrations.md
---
# Migrations

`dbx migrate` converts a project's tooling config from another tool to
**Oxc** (Oxfmt + Oxlint), or folds an existing Oxc/Vite config into
`dbx.config.*`. Migrations are pluggable — adding a source tool is a
matter of implementing one interface.

```sh
dbx migrate:list                       # what's available + detected
dbx migrate --from biome               # dry-run
dbx migrate --from biome --write       # writes the oxc config
dbx migrate --from biome --target vite --write
dbx migrate --from biome --from prettier --write  # several sources
dbx migrate --from oxc --write         # fold .oxfmtrc/.oxlintrc into dbx.config
dbx migrate --from all                 # every detected source
dbx migrate --check                    # CI: exit 1 when the oxc config is stale
dbx migrate --from eslint --online --write   # flat config via @oxlint/migrate
```

`dbx migrate` is a dry-run unless you pass `--write` (or `--check`). `--from`
is repeatable; `--from all` (or omitting it) selects every detected source.

## Sources

| Source     | Notes                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `biome`    | Formatter options, `files.includes` negations → `ignorePatterns`, **`organizeImports.groups` → Oxfmt `sortImports`**, and a curated Biome → Oxlint rule map. |
| `prettier` | Prettier-compatible options transfer directly; Tailwind/PackageJson plugins detected; `.prettierignore` → `ignorePatterns`.                                  |
| `eslint`   | JSON configs map rule names + severities (`@typescript-eslint/*` → `typescript/*`); JS/flat configs use `@oxlint/migrate` with `--online --write`.           |
| `dprint`   | `dprint.json` layout + TypeScript options → Oxfmt.                                                                                                           |
| `oxc`      | Folds `.oxfmtrc.json` / `.oxlintrc.json` into `dbx.config.*`'s `toolchain.fmt.oxc` / `toolchain.lint.oxc`; `dbx sync` manages them again.                    |
| `vite`     | Folds a hand-written `vite.config.*` into `dbx.config.*`'s `toolchain.vite` (see below).                                                                     |

## Targets

* `--target files` (default) — writes `.oxfmtrc.json` and `.oxlintrc.json`.
* `--target vite` — folds the result into an existing `vite.config.ts`
  (inserting/replacing `fmt` and `lint`), which is what Vite+ reads.
* The `oxc` source always targets `dbx.config.*` (`toolchain.fmt.oxc` /
  `toolchain.lint.oxc`); `--target` does not apply.

## Recursive migration

By default `dbx migrate` only touches the root (`--cwd`, or the current
directory). `--recursive` walks the discovered projects under the root and
migrates each one that has a **detected source**:

```sh
dbx migrate --from biome --from prettier --recursive --write
```

On an interactive terminal it first asks which projects to migrate with a
multi-select — every candidate is listed by its relative path (with its package
name as a hint), plus an **All projects** option. Non-interactive runs (piped
output, CI, or `--json`) migrate every candidate without prompting. A project is
a candidate when a migration matching `--from` (or any migration, for `all`/no
`--from`) is detected in its directory — so a workspace with its own
`biome.json` or `vite.config.*` is included, and one without is skipped.

## `vite.config`

The `vite` source moves a hand-written `vite.config.*` into `dbx.config.*`'s
`toolchain.vite`, so the whole Vite+ config lives in the one hand-authored config
and `dbx sync` writes a thin `vite.config.ts` shim that resolves it at load time:

```sh
dbx migrate --from vite          # dry-run: shows what would fold in
dbx migrate --from vite --write  # folds the object into toolchain.vite
dbx sync                         # writes the managed vite.config.ts shim
```

It also adds `/vite.config.ts` to `toolchain.vite.fmt.ignorePatterns`, so Oxfmt
leaves the generated shim alone (otherwise `vp fmt` would rewrite it and
`dbx sync --check` would report drift).

It extracts the object literal passed to `defineConfig(...)` (or the
default-exported object) with a string-aware, balanced-paren scanner and
text-splices it into the nearest `dbx.config.*`: it inserts `vite: { ... }`, or
**deep-merges** into an existing `toolchain.vite` (nested objects are combined;
arrays and scalars from the vite config win), so its settings are kept. A
previous `config: false` opt-out is flipped to `config: true`, since the
hand-written file is being removed. When the config references imports, plugins
or any non-literal expression it is reported as **unmapped** and nothing is
written, rather than emitting broken output. A JSON `dbx.config.json` is also
left alone (the object is folded by hand).

When the project has a `vite.config.*` but **no** `dbx.config.*` (a workspace
that never had one), the migration creates a fresh `dbx.config.ts` holding the
folded `toolchain.vite`, wrapped in `defineConfig` from `@deltabox/toolchain`
(like the scaffold). A workspace resolves that import through the root's
installed dependency — in a self-hosted repo, via a root `portal:.` self-link.

The now-redundant `vite.config.*` is removed and recreated by `dbx sync` as a
shim that imports `defineConfig` from the project's own Vite package (`vite` or
`vite-plus`, detected from `package.json`). Pass `--ignore-vite-config-file` to
keep the original file.

### Nested configs

In a monorepo, pass `--recursive` to fold **each workspace's** own
`vite.config.*` into that workspace's `dbx.config.*` (creating one when it is
missing) instead of the root's:

```sh
dbx migrate --from vite --recursive --write
```

Without `--recursive`, only the root's `vite.config.*` is migrated and nested
ones are left alone. Detection is per project root (a directory with a
`package.json` or `dbx.config.*`, up to five levels deep), so a `vite.config.*`
in a deeper subdirectory of a project is not discovered. A workspace with no
`dbx.config.*` gets a fresh one holding just its `toolchain.vite`; it inherits
the rest of the config from the nearest ancestor at load time.

## Post-migration sync

A `--write` run finishes by regenerating the project's toolchain-managed files
(the same files `dbx sync` writes) for every project it changed — so a migrated
project is immediately consistent, eg. the managed `vite.config.ts` shim appears
right after folding a hand-written config. Two flags narrow that step:

| Flag                     | Effect                                                                    |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ignore-managed-files` | Skip the post-migration sync entirely; managed files are left untouched.  |
| `--ignore-changelog`     | Run the sync but drop the `changelog` task (workflows, commitlint, hook). |

The sync only runs after `--write`; a dry-run reports what it would do instead.

## Package scripts

`dbx migrate` migrates the tooling **files**; the matching `package.json` scripts
are a small follow-up. The common swaps:

| Before                   | After                       |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `biome format --write .` | `dbx fmt`                   |
| `biome check --fix .`    | `dbx lint --fix`            |
| `turbo build`            | `dbx run -r build`          |
| `turbo typecheck`        | `dbx run -r typecheck`      |
| `turbo test`             | `dbx run -r test`           |
| `turbo dev`              | `dbx run -r --parallel dev` |

Then drop `@biomejs/biome` + `turbo` (and `biome.json` + `turbo.json`) and add
`@deltabox/toolchain` + `vite-plus`. The full walkthrough — recommended scripts,
the dependency diff and per-workspace tasks — is on the
[Package scripts](/guide/scripts) page.

## CI check

`--check` runs the migrations without writing and exits non-zero when a target
file is missing or differs from what the migration would produce, so a pipeline
can require that a repo is fully on Oxc:

```sh
dbx migrate --check || echo "still on Biome/ESLint — run migrate --write"
```

`--online` allows network access: the ESLint migration shells out to
`@oxlint/migrate` to evaluate JS/flat configs (it writes `.oxlintrc.json`, so it
runs only together with `--write`).

## Honest output

Anything that cannot be mapped faithfully is reported instead of dropped:

```
unmapped (7):
  - organizeImports !lucide*: negated group members are approximated
  - linter.rules.suspicious.noUnknownAtRules: no Oxlint equivalent
```

## Programmatic

```ts
import { listMigrations, detectMigrations, runMigration } from '@deltabox/toolchain/migrate';

const detected = detectMigrations(process.cwd());
const result = await runMigration('biome', { cwd: process.cwd(), target: 'vite', write: true });
console.log(result.unmapped);
```

## Notes

`oxfmt --migrate biome`-style tools cover formatter options only; the pieces the
upstream tools skip (Biome `organizeImports`, Biome linter rules, Dprint) are
handled here.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/api.md
---
# Programmatic API

Every surface the CLI and the extension use is also importable. The umbrella
package re-exports the config model + sync runner and every workspace package, so
a consumer can import the whole surface from the root or a single package through
a subpath.

## Where to start

* [Umbrella (`@deltabox/toolchain`)](/guide/api/umbrella) — the root exports and
  the namespaced packages.
* [Subpath exports](/guide/api/subpath-exports) — the per-package entry points.
* [Package reference](/guide/api/package-reference) — every package's public
  exports.
* [Logging](/guide/api/logging) — the shared logger.
* [Examples](/guide/api/examples) — short, copy-pasteable recipes.
* [Registering commands](/guide/api/registering-commands) — wire
  `ToolchainCommand[]` onto a commander program.

```ts
import { defineConfig, loadToolchainConfig, runSync, defaultSyncTasks } from '@deltabox/toolchain';

const { config, tokens, projectType } = await loadToolchainConfig(process.cwd());
await runSync({ tasks: defaultSyncTasks(), cwd: process.cwd(), config, tokens, projectType });
```

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/config.md
---

# Config types

The toolchain has three configuration surfaces, all derived from the same Zod
model:

* **Programmatic** — `defineConfig({ toolchain: { ... } })` in
  `dbx.config.ts`; typed as `ToolchainConfig` (see the
  [TypeScript guide](/guide/typescript)).
* **CLI** — the `dbx` command options, generated from the command descriptors;
  see the [CLI reference](/config/cli).
* **Environment** — schema leaves can opt into env vars with
  `.meta({ env })`; see the [environment reference](/config/env) and the
  [Config Generator](/guide/config-generator/).

The exhaustive object reference is [dbx.config](/config/reference); the editor
JSON Schema is [config.schema.json](https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/config.schema.json).

## Fields

Every generated page uses the same `ConfigMeta` fields: `description`,
`required`, `deprecated`, `example`, `secret`, `scope`, `public`,
`defaultValue`, plus the env fields `env` and `path`.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/config/reference.md
---

# dbx.config

A `dbx.config.ts` file exports `{ toolchain: { ...sections } }`: the
`@deltabox/toolchain` settings live under the `toolchain` key. Every
section is **opt-in by presence** (see [Configuration](/guide/config/opt-in-by-presence)):
define it to enable it, omit it to leave that area untouched.

> Generated from the Zod config schema — do not edit by hand.
> Run `yarn config:generate`.

## `project`

Project metadata: canonical `package.json` fields and template tokens (shared fields are inherited by workspaces).

### `type`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

The project kind (detected when omitted).

### `name`

* **Type**: `string`

The unscoped project name (written as `<scope>/<name>`).

### `scope`

* **Type**: `string`

The npm scope, eg. `@acme`.

### `author`

* **Type**: `string`

Package author (`package.json` `author`).

### `license`

* **Type**: `string`

SPDX license id (`package.json` `license`).

### `homepage`

* **Type**: `string`

Project homepage (`package.json` `homepage`).

### `repo`

* **Type**: `string`

Repository URL (`package.json` `repository`). For a workspace it also resolves to the workspace path (`repository.directory`).

### `nodeVersion`

* **Type**: `string`

Node version for CI/templates, eg. `22` (not `package.json` `engines`).

### `packageManager`

* **Type**: `string`

Package manager name, written as `<name>@<version>` (default `yarn`).

### `packageManagerVersion`

* **Type**: `string`

Package manager version, eg. `4.17.1`.

### `description`

* **Type**: `string`

One-line description (`package.json` `description`).

### `inherit`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Inherit the parent project metadata (default true). Set false to keep this project entirely independent of the root config.

## `ci`

GitHub Actions workflows to generate (CI, release, issues, changelog, sync).

### `ci`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

The CI checks workflow (`ci.yml`).

### `changelog`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

The changelog/version workflow (`changelog.yml`) plus the changelog pipeline config (versioning, VS Code settings, commitlint).

### `release`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

The release workflow (`release.yml`).

### `issues`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

The issue-title workflow (`issues.yml`).

### `sync`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

The toolchain sync workflow (`sync.yml`).

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `fmt`

Formatter configuration: Oxc/Biome configs, editor defaults and source-tool options.

### `vscode`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

Add project-scoped VS Code settings: `true`/`false` or `{ overrides, exclude }` (default false; existing keys are kept).

### `oxc`

* **Type**: `Record<string, unknown>`
* **Default**: `{}`

Oxfmt options. `toolchain.vite.fmt` overrides these (deep merge).

### `biome`

* **Type**: `Record<string, unknown>`
* **Default**: `{}`

Biome formatter options (merged into the generated `biome.json`).

### `prettier`

* **Type**: `Record<string, unknown>`
* **Default**: `{}`

Prettier options (editor defaults/migrations).

### `dprint`

* **Type**: `Record<string, unknown>`
* **Default**: `{}`

Dprint options (editor defaults/migrations).

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `lint`

Linter configuration: Oxc/Biome configs, editor defaults and ESLint options.

### `vscode`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

Add project-scoped VS Code settings: `true`/`false` or `{ overrides, exclude }` (default false; existing keys are kept).

### `oxc`

* **Type**: `Record<string, unknown>`
* **Default**: `{}`

Oxlint options. `toolchain.vite.lint` overrides these (deep merge).

### `biome`

* **Type**: `Record<string, unknown>`
* **Default**: `{}`

Biome linter options (merged into the generated `biome.json`).

### `eslint`

* **Type**: `Record<string, unknown>`
* **Default**: `{}`

ESLint options (editor defaults/migrations).

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `biome`

Biome config generation (for consumers that still want a `biome.json`).

* **Deprecated**: use `toolchain.fmt.biome` / `toolchain.lint.biome`. Still writes `biome.json`.

### `vscode`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Write the Biome VS Code settings (default true).

### `overrides`

* **Type**: `Record<string, unknown>`
* **Default**: `{}`

Deep-merged over the generated `biome.json` (arrays union).

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `tsconfig`

Workspace tsconfig generation (path aliases + project references).

### `glob`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

Glob(s) for the workspace default tsconfig files. Defaults to matching every `defaultFile` recursively.

### `exclude`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

Glob(s) to exclude from `glob`. Defaults to the common ignored paths (`node_modules`, `.dbx`, `dist`, `build`, ...).

### `gitignore`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Also respect `.gitignore` files (root + nested) when matching `glob` (default true).

### `refs`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Wire project references (default false).

### `composite`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Emit `composite: true` (default false).

### `aliases`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Inject path aliases (default true).

### `indent`

* **Type**: `number`

JSON indentation (default 4).

### `rootFile`

* **Type**: `string`

The workspaces tsconfig file name that holds `paths` + `references` (default `tsconfig.workspaces.json`).

### `defaultFile`

* **Type**: `string`

The workspace default tsconfig file name that the generator expands (default `tsconfig.default.json`).

### `buildFile`

* **Type**: `string`

The workspace build tsconfig file name (default `tsconfig.build.json`).

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `templates`

Template sources / scaffolding.

### `sources`

* **Type**: `Array<any>`

Extra sources on top of the builtin + registry sources.

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `registry`

Registry source allow/deny policies (templates + providers).

### `templates`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

Allow/deny globs for template sources and registries.

### `providers`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

Allow/deny globs for provider sources and registries.

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `catalogs`

Package catalogs written to the package manager catalog file (`catalog:`).

### `packages`

* **Type**: `Record<string, unknown>`
* **Default**: `{}`

The default catalog: package name -> version range.

### `named`

* **Type**: `Record<string, unknown>`
* **Default**: `{}`

Named catalogs (Yarn `catalogs:` / pnpm `catalogs:`): name -> packages.

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `vite`

The full Vite+ config; `dbx sync` writes the root `vite.config.ts` from it.

### `config`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Write the managed Vite config (default true). A string sets its file name/path (relative to the project, or absolute).

### `fmt`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

Oxfmt options; `true` uses the toolchain defaults.

### `lint`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

Oxlint options; `true` uses the toolchain defaults.

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `watch`

Watch behaviour for `dbx watch`.

### `debounce`

* **Type**: `number`

Debounce window in ms (default 150).

### `exclude`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

Glob(s) excluded from watching. Defaults to the common ignored paths (`node_modules`, `.dbx`, `dist`, `build`, ...).

### `gitignore`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Also respect `.gitignore` files (root + nested) when watching (default true).

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `logger`

Logging level, colours and prefix for toolchain output.

### `level`

* **Type**: `string`

Minimum level to print (default `info`).

### `color`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Force colours on/off (default: on; `--no-color` disables).

### `name`

* **Type**: `string`

Prefix non-indented lines with `<name>:` (default `dbx`).

### `suppress`

* **Type**: `any`
* **Default**: `{}`

Warning/error id, message substring, or `/regex/` to silence (single value or array).

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## `providers`

Provider command behaviour (eg. colour for the passthrough commands).

### `color`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Force provider command colours on/off (default: inherit the logger).

### `enabled`

* **Type**: `boolean`

Enable/disable this section (default: enabled when defined).

## Full example

```ts [dbx.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from '@deltabox/toolchain';

export default defineConfig({
    toolchain: {
        project: { type: 'monorepo-root', name: 'acme', scope: '@acme' },
        ci: { ci: true, release: true, changelog: { branches: { main: 'main' } } },
        tsconfig: { refs: true },
        templates: { sources: [{ type: 'local', locate: './templates', kind: 'application' }] },
        vite: { fmt: { semi: true, singleQuote: true }, test: { include: ['src/**/*.test.ts'] } },
        watch: { debounce: 150 },
    },
});
```

# CLI reference

Generated from the same `ToolchainCommand` descriptors the `dbx` binary
registers. Run `yarn config:docs` after changing a command.

| Command | Description |
| ------- | ----------- |
| [`dbx projects`](#projects) | Discover projects and write .dbx/toolchain/projects.json. |
| [`dbx sync`](#sync) | Regenerate every managed file from dbx.config.*. |
| [`dbx watch`](#watch) | Sync once, then watch key files and re-sync on change. |
| [`dbx reset`](#reset) | Remove generated files, the .dbx/toolchain manifest and/or the dbx config from a project. |
| [`dbx providers`](#providers) | List the tooling providers (Vite+, ...) and their commands. |
| [`dbx tsconfig`](#tsconfig) | Generate workspace tsconfig.json files from the default tsconfig (aliases + references). |
| [`dbx cleanup`](#cleanup) | Remove build artifacts (*.tsbuildinfo, dist/). |
| [`dbx cleanup:turbo`](#cleanup-turbo) | Remove the turbo cache (.turbo/). |
| [`dbx workflow`](#workflow) | Trigger one or more generated GitHub workflows (via `gh workflow run`). |
| [`dbx changelog`](#changelog) | Scan commits, derive the semver bump and update the CHANGELOG.md files + versions. |
| [`dbx migrate`](#migrate) | Migrate Biome / ESLint / Prettier / Dprint / Oxc config, or fold vite.config.\* into dbx.config. |
| [`dbx migrate:list`](#migrate-list) | List the registered migrations and whether each is detected. |
| [`dbx project:init`](#project-init) | Scaffold a single-package TypeScript project. |
| [`dbx project:init:monorepo`](#project-init-monorepo) | Scaffold a monorepo root (add --example for one example workspace). |
| [`dbx project:init:workspace`](#project-init-workspace) | Scaffold a monorepo workspace package into an existing monorepo root. |
| [`dbx project:config`](#project-config) | Generate dbx.config.ts for existing projects that are missing one. |

## `dbx projects`

Discover projects and write .dbx/toolchain/projects.json.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Root to scan (default: cwd).
* `--max-depth ‹n›` — Max directory depth. (default: `5`)
* `--no-write` — Do not write the graph file.
* `--json` — Print the graph as JSON.

## `dbx sync`

Regenerate every managed file from dbx.config.\*.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `-q, --quiet` — Only log errors.
* `--check` — Do not write; fail if files are out of date.
* `--watch` — Keep running and re-sync on change.
* `--recursive` — Sync every discovered dbx project in dependency order.
* `--force` — Run even when no dbx.config.\* is present.
* `--json` — Print the sync result (including removed files) as JSON.

## `dbx watch`

Sync once, then watch key files and re-sync on change.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `-q, --quiet` — Only log errors.
* `--force` — Run even when no dbx.config.\* is present.

## `dbx reset`

Remove generated files, the .dbx/toolchain manifest and/or the dbx config from a project.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--recursive` — Reset every discovered project under the root.
* `--include ‹pattern...›` — Only projects matching these patterns (glob or substring).
* `--exclude ‹pattern...›` — Skip projects matching these patterns (glob or substring).
* `--generated` — Remove only the generated/managed files.
* `--manifest` — Remove only the .dbx/toolchain directory.
* `--config` — Also remove dbx.config.\*.
* `--all` — Remove generated files, the manifest and the config.
* `--dry-run` — Report what would be removed without deleting.
* `--json` — Print the result as JSON.

## `dbx providers`

List the tooling providers (Vite+, ...) and their commands.

* `--json` — Print the providers (with actions) as JSON.

## `dbx tsconfig`

Generate workspace tsconfig.json files from the default tsconfig (aliases + references).

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Repo root to scan (default: cwd).
* `--no-aliases` — Skip path aliases.
* `--composite` — Emit composite + references.
* `--refs` — Wire project references.
* `-i, --indent ‹n›` — JSON indentation.
* `--glob ‹glob...›` — Glob(s) for the default tsconfig files.
* `--exclude ‹glob...›` — Glob(s) to exclude (on top of the common ignored paths).
* `--no-gitignore` — Do not respect .gitignore files.
* `--default-file ‹file›` — Default tsconfig file name.
* `--build-file ‹file›` — Build tsconfig file name.
* `--root-file ‹file›` — Workspaces tsconfig file name.

## `dbx cleanup`

Remove build artifacts (\*.tsbuildinfo, dist/).

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Directory to clean (default: cwd).
* `--pattern ‹glob...›` — Override the match globs.

## `dbx cleanup:turbo`

Remove the turbo cache (.turbo/).

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Directory to clean (default: cwd).

## `dbx workflow`

Trigger one or more generated GitHub workflows (via `gh workflow run`).

* `[workflows]` — Workflow ids or file names (default: every enabled workflow).
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--ref ‹ref›` — Git ref to run the workflow on.
* `--gh ‹cmd›` — The gh executable (default: gh).

## `dbx changelog`

Scan commits, derive the semver bump and update the CHANGELOG.md files + versions.

* `--range ‹range›` — Git revision range to scan.
* `--dry-run` — Print the proposed entry without writing.
* `--version ‹semver›` — Override the version.
* `--base-version ‹semver›` — Bump from this version instead.
* `--processing-method ‹method›` — `latest` (default), `all`, or a git range.
* `--format-only` — Only regroup existing changelogs.
* `--no-package-changes-section` — Skip the package-changes footer.

## `dbx migrate`

Migrate Biome / ESLint / Prettier / Dprint / Oxc config, or fold vite.config.\* into dbx.config.

* `--from ‹tool›` — Source tool (repeatable): biome | eslint | prettier | dprint | oxc | vite | all.
* `--to ‹tool›` — Target tool (default: oxc). (default: `oxc`)
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--recursive` — Also migrate the discovered projects under the root (default: root only).
* `--write` — Write the files (default: dry-run).
* `--dry-run` — Do not write anything (default).
* `--check` — CI: exit non-zero when the oxc config is stale.
* `--target ‹target›` — files (default) | vite.
* `--online` — Allow network (e.g. @oxlint/migrate).
* `--ignore-vite-config-file` — Do not remove the folded `vite.config.*`.
* `--ignore-managed-files` — Skip the post-migration sync (leave the toolchain-managed files as-is).
* `--ignore-changelog` — Skip the changelog task in the post-migration sync.
* `--json` — Print the result as JSON.

## `dbx migrate:list`

List the registered migrations and whether each is detected.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--json` — Print as JSON.

## `dbx project:init`

Scaffold a single-package TypeScript project.

* `-n, --name ‹name›` — Project name.
* `-s, --scope ‹scope›` — npm scope, eg. @acme.
* `-o, --out ‹dir›` — Output directory (default: cwd).
* `--package-manager ‹pm›` — Package manager: yarn (default) | pnpm | npm | bun.
* `--no-config` — Skip the dbx.config.ts file.
* `--type ‹type›` — Project type: project | monorepo-root | monorepo-workspace.

## `dbx project:init:monorepo`

Scaffold a monorepo root (add --example for one example workspace).

* `-n, --name ‹name›` — Project name.
* `-s, --scope ‹scope›` — npm scope, eg. @acme.
* `-o, --out ‹dir›` — Output directory (default: cwd).
* `--example` — Also scaffold one example workspace package.
* `--package-manager ‹pm›` — Package manager: yarn (default) | pnpm | npm | bun.
* `--no-config` — Skip the dbx.config.ts file.
* `--type ‹type›` — Project type: project | monorepo-root | monorepo-workspace.

## `dbx project:init:workspace`

Scaffold a monorepo workspace package into an existing monorepo root.

* `-n, --name ‹name›` — Workspace package name (unscoped).
* `-s, --scope ‹scope›` — npm scope, eg. @acme.
* `-r, --root ‹dir›` — Monorepo root (default: cwd).
* `-d, --dir ‹dir›` — Workspace dir relative to the root (default: packages/\<name>).
* `--package-manager ‹pm›` — Package manager: yarn (default) | pnpm | npm | bun.
* `--no-config` — Skip the dbx.config.ts file.
* `--type ‹type›` — Project type: project | monorepo-root | monorepo-workspace.

## `dbx project:config`

Generate dbx.config.ts for existing projects that are missing one.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Root to scan (default: cwd).
* `--include ‹pattern...›` — Only projects matching these patterns (glob or substring).
* `--exclude ‹pattern...›` — Skip projects matching these patterns (glob or substring).
* `--type ‹type›` — Force a project type for every config.
* `--force` — Overwrite configs that already exist.
* `--dry-run` — Report what would be written without writing.
* `--json` — Print the result as JSON.

## `dbx template:list`

List templates (builtin + local + opted-in online sources).

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--online` — Resolve online sources (npm/git).
* `--offline` — Force offline (skip npm/git).
* `--global` — Only the global registry templates.
* `--kind ‹kind›` — project | workspace | application | folder | tooling | pipeline.
* `--registry` — List only the .dbx/toolchain/templates.json sources.
* `--json` — Print the templates as JSON.

## `dbx template:init`

Write a template.json to a directory, making it a local template.

* `[dir]` — Directory (default: cwd).
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--kind ‹kind›` — project | workspace | application | folder | tooling | pipeline.
* `--name ‹name›` — Display name (default: folder name).
* `--id ‹id›` — Stable template id (default: folder name).
* `--description ‹text›` — Description.
* `--var ‹pair...›` — Variable name\[:default] (repeatable).
* `--tag ‹tag...›` — Tag (repeatable).
* `--force` — Overwrite an existing template.json.
* `--add` — Also record the folder in .dbx/toolchain/templates.json.
* `--no-global` — Do not also store the template in the global registry.
* `--json` — Print the manifest as JSON.

## `dbx template:add`

Record a template source in .dbx/toolchain/templates.json.

* `‹source›` — local path | git URL | @scope/create | type:locate
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--type ‹type›` — Force: builtin | local | npm | git | vite-plus | remote.
* `--name ‹name›` — Display name.
* `--id ‹id›` — Stable template id (default: inferred).
* `--kind ‹kind›` — project | workspace | application | folder | tooling | pipeline.
* `--ref ‹ref›` — Git branch/tag/commit.
* `--registry ‹url›` — Custom npm registry (default: the project package manager).
* `--subdir ‹dir›` — Subdirectory within the source.
* `--no-global` — Do not also register the source in the global registry.
* `--json` — Print the updated registry as JSON.

## `dbx template:remove`

Remove a source from .dbx/toolchain/templates.json.

* `‹id›` — Source id or type:locate.
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--global` — Remove the template from the global registry.
* `--json` — Print the registry as JSON.

## `dbx template:registry`

Manage the global template search paths (and sync them to the VS Code setting).

* `--list` — List the resolved search paths (default).
* `--add ‹path...›` — Add global search path(s).
* `--remove ‹path...›` — Remove global search path(s).
* `--set ‹path...›` — Replace the global search paths.
* `--clear` — Reset the global search paths to the default.
* `--vscode-dir ‹dir›` — Record the VS Code user dir (its settings.json holds the paths).
* `--json` — Print the resolved config as JSON.

## `dbx registry`

List or manage the template/provider registries.

* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--kind ‹kind›` — What --add/--remove manages: templates | providers.
* `--add ‹path›` — Add a registry path (or remote URL).
* `--remove ‹path›` — Remove a registry path.
* `--set ‹path...›` — Replace the registry search paths.
* `--clear` — Clear the registry search paths.
* `--scope ‹scope›` — project | global (default: global).
* `--json` — Print the registries as JSON.

## `dbx template:info`

Show one template by id.

* `‹id›` — The template id.
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--online` — Resolve online sources.
* `--json` — Print the template as JSON (the default).

## `dbx create`

Scaffold a project from a template (builtin, local or Vite+).

* `-t, --template ‹id›` — Template id (see template:list).
* `--kind ‹kind›` — project | workspace | application | folder | tooling | pipeline.
* `-n, --name ‹name›` — Project / package name.
* `-s, --scope ‹scope›` — npm scope, eg. @acme.
* `-o, --out ‹dir›` — Output directory (default: cwd).
* `--cwd ‹dir›` — Project root (default: cwd).
* `--var ‹pair...›` — Template variables as key=value (repeatable).
* `--action ‹id...›` — Action id to run after scaffolding (repeatable).
* `--online` — Resolve online templates too.
* `--json` — Print the result as JSON.

# Environment variables

The toolchain config is file/CLI backed; a schema leaf opts into an
environment variable with `.meta({ env: "..." })` (see the
[Config Generator](/guide/config-generator/describe-a-scope)).

No environment-backed toolchain settings are declared.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config/defineconfig.md
---
# `defineConfig`

`defineConfig` is an identity helper that gives the file full type-checking and
autocomplete (it mirrors Vite's `defineConfig`). Like Vite, the argument may be a
plain object, a promise, or a sync/async callback — the loader resolves it, so a
config can do async work before returning `{ toolchain }`:

```ts [dbx.config.ts]
export default defineConfig(async () => {
    const { readFile } = await import('node:fs/promises');
    const version = (await readFile('./VERSION', 'utf-8')).trim();

    return {
        toolchain: {
            project: { name: 'acme', nodeVersion: version },
        },
    };
});
```

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/changelog/branches.md
---
# Branches

`ci.changelog.branches.main` and `ci.changelog.branches.dev` pick which branches
the generated workflows target. Each accepts a glob or an array of globs:

| Branch | Drives                                                                         | Default              |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
| `main` | The **CI** workflow (push), the **release** workflow, and the release PR base. | `['main']`           |
| `dev`  | The **changelog/version** workflow (push).                                     | none — reuses `main` |

`dev` has **no default**: when it is omitted the changelog workflow runs on
`main` (so a single-branch repo needs no `dev`). Set it for a `dev` → `main`
flow:

```ts
ci: { changelog: { branches: { main: 'main', dev: 'dev' } } }
// or multiple branches per purpose:
ci: { changelog: { branches: { main: ['main', 'release/**'], dev: ['dev', 'next'] } } }
```

The `sync` workflow runs on both. Any per-workflow `pushBranches` override (eg.
`ci.release.pushBranches`) still wins.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/changelog/cli.md
---
# CLI

```sh
dbx changelog                       # bump + write (uses ci.changelog.versioning)
dbx changelog --dry-run             # preview the root entry
dbx changelog --range v1.2.0..HEAD  # scan a specific range
dbx changelog --version 2.0.0       # force a version (retags the changelogs)
dbx changelog --format-only         # regroup existing changelogs, no bump
```

The command reads `ci.changelog` and falls back to the manual
`toolchain.changelog` pipeline options (commitlint, versioning, vscode). This
lets a project keep manual/API changelog runs without enabling the CI workflow;
`ci.changelog` inherits the same options when it does not override them.

The generated `changelog` workflow runs `dbx changelog --range …` on every push
to the `dev` branches (or `main` when `dev` is unset), so versioning is applied
from CI as well as locally.

`dbx workflow [id…]` triggers the generated GitHub workflows through
`gh workflow run`; with no ids it triggers every workflow you declared under
`toolchain.ci`.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator/cli-commands.md
---
# CLI commands

`configCommands({ engine, defaults })` returns `ToolchainCommand[]` (register them
on your commander program with `@deltabox/toolchain/cli`):

| Command           | Writes                                       |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `config:env`      | `.env.example`                               |
| `config:types`    | config types (`--env` also writes env types) |
| `config:json`     | `config.json` (metadata)                     |
| `config:schema`   | `config.schema.json`                         |
| `config:markdown` | the markdown reference                       |
| `config:cli`      | `cli-options.json`                           |
| `config:all`      | everything, under one output directory       |

```ts
import { configCommands } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

const commands = configCommands({
    engine,
    defaults: { typesDir: 'packages/shared/src/types', docsDir: 'docs/reference' },
});
// register `commands` on your commander program
```

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/changelog/commitlint.md
---
# commitlint

By default the generated `commitlint.config.mjs` lives at the project root. Set
`ci.changelog.commitlint.dir` to write it elsewhere:

```ts
ci: {
    changelog: {
        commitlint: {
            dir: '.config';
        }
    }
} // -> .config/commitlint.config.mjs
```

When a custom dir is set, the generated husky hook and the CI commitlint step
both pass `--config <dir>/commitlint.config.mjs`, so commitlint finds it. Note
that editor tooling that discovers the config by convention (eg. the
Conventional Commits VS Code extension, which loads from the repo root) expects
the config at the root — keep the default unless you have a reason to move it.

`commitlint.types` and `commitlint.scopes` are the allowed Conventional-Commits
types/scopes:

```ts
ci: {
    changelog: {
        commitlint: {
            types: ['feat', 'fix', 'docs', 'chore'],
            scopes: ['api', 'web', 'deps'],
        },
    },
}
```

## Disabling commitlint

Set `ci.changelog.commitlint: false` (or `{ enabled: false }`) to generate
changelogs **without** the Conventional-Commits rules. The changelog workflow is
still generated, but dbx writes no `commitlint.config.mjs`, no husky hook and no
commitlint step in the CI workflow.

The changelog then falls back to a coarse grouping: commits are hoisted into
`Major changes`, `Minor changes` and `Patch changes` buckets (breaking commits
and `feat:` go to major/minor; everything else is a patch), while the package
changes section (eg. new packages) is kept. This is intentionally less detailed
than the rule/scope grouping, but it works with any commit-message style.

> The extension's `No "exports" main defined in … conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits …`
> error is an upstream commitlint bug (ESM-only parser preset), not a config
> discovery problem. See [Troubleshooting](/guide/changelog/troubleshooting).

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config/config-file-names.md
---
# Config file names

The loader looks for, in order:

```
dbx.config.ts
dbx.config.mts
dbx.config.js
dbx.config.mjs
dbx.config.cjs
dbx.config.json
```

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator/create-the-engine.md
---
# Create the engine

Bind the scopes, an env prefix, the base group and the project root once:

```ts
import { createConfigEngine } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';

export const engine = createConfigEngine({
    schema: {
        server: serverConfig,
        frontend: frontendConfig,
        cli: cliConfig,
    },
    envPrefix: 'MYAPP_',
    baseGroup: 'base', // the flat fields hoisted out of the nested groups
    root: process.cwd(),
    // Optional: custom env-name -> dotted-path derivation (eg. dual prefixes).
    envPathOf: env =>
        env
            .replace(/^(MYAPP_|VITE_)/, '')
            .toLowerCase()
            .replace(/_/g, '.'),
});
```

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator/describe-a-scope.md
---
# Describe a scope

Each scope is a Zod object. Leaves that are backed by an environment variable
carry an `.meta()` describing that variable:

```ts
import { z } from 'zod';

export const serverConfig = z.object({
    base: z.object({
        port: z.number().default(3000).meta({
            env: 'MYAPP_PORT',
            description: 'HTTP port',
        }),
        host: z.string().default('0.0.0.0').meta({
            env: 'MYAPP_HOST',
            description: 'Bind address',
        }),
    }),
    auth: z.object({
        password: z.string().meta({
            env: 'MYAPP_AUTH_PASSWORD',
            description: 'Admin password',
            required: true,
            secret: true,
        }),
        tokenTtl: z.number().default(3600).meta({
            env: 'MYAPP_AUTH_TOKEN_TTL',
            description: 'Session lifetime (seconds)',
        }),
    }),
});
```

`ConfigMeta` fields: `env`, `path` (dotted config path), `description`,
`required`, `deprecated`, `deprecationMessage`, `example`, `since`, `see`,
`remarks`, `experimental`, `alpha`, `beta`, `secret`, `scope`, `public` (safe to
expose to the browser) and `defaultValue` (when the resolved default differs
from the env default).

`required: true` adds `@required` and `- **Required**` above the markdown
`- **Type**` line. `deprecated: true` adds `@deprecated` / `- **Deprecated**`;
`deprecationMessage` supplies the text. `example` (string or array) adds one
`@example` tag/entry per value under `**Example(s):**`. `since` adds `@since` /
`- **Since**`, `see` adds `@see` / `- **See**` links, `remarks` adds `@remarks` /
`**Remarks:**`, and `experimental`/`alpha`/`beta` add their stability tags.

Each generator accepts the matching `include*` flag (all default `true`) to
suppress an annotation: `includeRequired`, `includeDeprecated`,
`includeExamples`, `includeSince`, `includeSee`, `includeRemarks`,
`includeExperimental`, `includeAlpha`, `includeBeta` — for example
`generateConfigTypes(..., { includeExamples: false })` or
`writeMarkdown(..., { includeDeprecated: false })`.

---

---
url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/api/examples.md
---
# Examples

```ts
// Vite+ provider
import { resolveVp, runVp, resolveVpCommand, VP_COMMANDS } from '@deltabox/toolchain/vite';
await runVp(['check'], { cwd: process.cwd() });
resolveVpCommand('i'); // 'install'

// Migrations
import { detectMigrations, runMigration } from '@deltabox/toolchain/migrate';
for (const m of detectMigrations(process.cwd())) await m.run({ cwd: process.cwd(), write: true });

// Templates
import { loadTemplates, scaffoldTemplate } from '@deltabox/toolchain/template';
const [template] = await loadTemplates({ cwd: process.cwd() });
if (template) await scaffoldTemplate(template, { cwd: './out', tokens: { name: 'acme' } });

// Providers (what the editor reads)
import { toolchainProviders } from '@deltabox/toolchain/providers';
console.log(toolchainProviders().map(p => p.id));

// Config engine
import { createConfigEngine } from '@deltabox/toolchain/config';
```

url: https://toolchain.deltabox.studio/guide/config-generator/generate.md
